question: Ticket 3213aed6b00c says 'In proofs_touching, unsealed staged proofs are added to the result, so reseal_all runs them and stages their first seal.', but outline 9.4.2.3.7.5 reads "Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Every red and every orphaned file is fixed; one unrelated to the work in hand is ticketed, and once it is, that crossing can go ahead." (9.4.2.3.7.5 states 'Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds...'. A newly added proof sealed red-first is a new red from the tester run, but the ticket description specifies only that the seal is staged, with no mention of ticket creation. The bounds note the hook script ruling is a separate ticket, but the clause 'Each run writes a ticket for every new red' would not demonstrably hold after the ticket is built as written unless ticket creation is explicitly ensured by the same change. The ticket's how-clause must state whether a ticket is created or explain why this red is exempt from 9.4.2.3.7.5's requirement.). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
why_it_blocks: the ticket and the component outline disagree; building it would build one of them wrong
answer: The ticket stands, and it serves 9.4.2.3.7.5. Today a newly added proof is never run at commit (census reads only proofs that already hold a validation), so its red is lost, which is what that line forbids. The reds this seals are red-first proofs, each brought by an open ticket whose PROVES names it: the already-open case of 9.4.2.3.7.5. A sealed red keeps the component red at component_color, so nothing is hidden. No ticket is created by the reseal, and none is needed.
